title: Nested IF...ELSE Statement

lines.explanation: Assigning the value 5 to the variable 'dice_score'

This is the outer 'If' condition. It checks if the value of 'dice_score' is less than 6. If this condition is true, the code will go the the inner 'If...else' conditions. In this case this condition is true since the value of dice_score is 5 which is less than 6.
This inner 'If' statement checks if the value is 1. If it is not true, it will jump to the next condition. In this case it is not true since the value of dice_score is 5

lines.code: print("Your score is 1. Please roll again.")

lines.explanation: This inner 'If' statement checks if the value is 2. If it is not true, it will jump to the next condition. In this case it is not true since the value of dice_score is 5

lines.code: print("Your score is 2. Please roll again.")

lines.explanation: This inner 'If' statement checks if the value is 3. If it is not true, it will jump to the next condition. In this case it is not true since the value of dice_score is 5

lines.code: print("Your score is 3. Please roll again.")

lines.explanation: This inner 'If' statement checks if the value is 4. If it is not true, it will jump to the next condition. In this case it is not true since the value of dice_score is 5

lines.code: print("Your score is 4. Please roll again.")

lines.explanation: Since all the above conditions are not true it will execute this 'else' statement by default.

lines.code: print("Your score is 5. Please roll again.")
lines.explanation: Since the else statement is executed, it will print out this string.
Imagine if the outer 'If' condition was not true, the code would have jumped to this 'elif' condition.

lines.code: print("It is a perfect dice score. Congratulations!")

lines.explanation: Again Imagine if none of the above conditions were true, the code would jump to this 'else' condition.

lines.code: print("It is an invalid dice score. The value should be between 1 and 6")
